problem: LLM agents struggle to retrieve relevant past experience at the right level of granularity when solving complex software engineering tasks, leading to misguided solutions.
approach: Aligns memory storage and retrieval with the agent's functional decomposition into subtasks rather than treating entire episodes as atomic units, improving instance-level matching.
contribution: Achieves +4.7 pp improvement in Pass@1 over vanilla agents, with gains scaling with interaction steps on SWE-bench Verified.

problem: Text-to-video generation fails to reliably synthesize multiple subjects with complex relations—subjects go missing and spatial relationships become misaligned.
approach: Decouples presence and alignment challenges via composition-aware attention: uses Subject-aware Condition Interpolation to enforce presence and Layout-forcing Attention Modulation to align spatial relations dynamically.
contribution: Boosts T2V-CompBench scores by 15.7% and 11.7% on two baselines with only 5% inference overhead, scaling to general T2V and compositional T2I.

problem: Agent benchmarks contain hidden validity flaws from interactions among user instructions, environments, tools, and evaluation protocols that confound model errors with benchmark artifacts.
approach: Decomposes tasks into four standardized components (User, Environment, Ground Truth, Evaluation) and applies hybrid rule-based and LLM-guided auditing to detect validity issues.
contribution: Achieves F1 scores 0.791-0.874 aligning with expert judgments and identifies missed issues in tau-bench; released AgentSuite platform.

problem: Test-time adaptation for vision-language models like CLIP suffers from optimization and inference stage mismatch when learning from pseudo labels generated by augmentations.
approach: Proposes self-ensembling strategy that adaptively emphasizes the test image itself over augmented views during both optimization and inference to obtain reliable pseudo labels.
contribution: USE framework and lightweight SE method outperform Test-Time Prompt Tuning; SE integrates as consistent booster with existing TTA methods.

problem: Dataset distillation compresses data but fails to preserve predictive patterns equally across demographic groups, causing fairness gaps independent of group imbalance.
approach: Identifies group-imbalance-agnostic barycenter of predictive information that induces similar representations across subgroups through cross-group alignment.
contribution: Reduces bias introduced by dataset distillation; method is compatible with existing distillation approaches and substantially improves fairness.

problem: Action chunking in vision-language-action models faces an inherent trade-off: longer horizons enable global foresight but impair fine-grained control, and vice versa.
approach: Mixture of Horizons segments action chunks into parallel streams with different horizons processed by a shared transformer, then fuses via a learned linear gate.
contribution: Enables adaptive dynamic inference with 2.5× higher throughput; achieves consistent gains on both simulated and real-world robotic tasks.

problem: Gradient-based optimization in class-incremental learning distorts decision boundaries from earlier tasks as new classes are added, creating a plasticity-stability dilemma.
approach: Externalizes plasticity into a binary synaptic matrix evolved via stochastic bit-flip updates with eligibility traces and collision signals that suppress cross-class interference.
contribution: Rivals gradient-based methods in exemplar-free settings; consistently boosts SOTA baselines as a lightweight plugin with mechanistic validation of geometric theory.

problem: Music-to-motion systems trained offline degrade in streaming where audio conditioning history becomes stale or unreliable and conditions change abruptly.
approach: Combines causal music encoder capturing rhythmic structure with diffusion-forcing sequence model trained under heterogeneous noise; hybrid schedule and history-guided sampler balance responsiveness and consistency.
contribution: Delivers stable long-horizon rollouts and sharper audio-motion alignment in real-time interactive system while maintaining causality and latency constraints.

problem: Masked Diffusion Models lack reliable self-correction mechanisms during inference—existing approaches require major architectural changes or imprecise quality proxies.
approach: PRISM applies lightweight plug-in remasking at inference: defines self-correction loss that provably learns per-token quality scores without RL or verifier.
contribution: Advances MDM inference across domains and scales (Sudoku, text-170M, code-8B); provides open-source implementation.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models degrade under distribution shifts because behavior representations suffer from short-horizon temporal fragmentation and static execution alignment.
approach: BehaviorVLA uses causal Mamba to encode long-horizon trajectories into unified behavior representation and phase-conditioned decoder to align actions with task progress.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on RoboTwin 2.0 (58%), LIBERO (98%), CALVIN (4.36); sim-to-real transfer matches OpenVLA-OFT with only 50% of data.

problem: Time series forecasting loss functions use point-wise Euclidean metrics that ignore the geometric structure of probability distributions, leading to suboptimal uncertainty quantification.
approach: InfoGeo Loss grounds loss in information geometry with three components: distribution parameterization with learnable statistics, Fisher information metric on manifolds, and Bregman divergence for asymmetry.
contribution: Achieves 6.8% MSE and 5.3% MAE improvement on average across seven datasets with five architectures; includes theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: 3D assembly methods treat the problem as pure pose estimation without leveraging holistic shape context, failing to handle missing geometry or infer plausible completions.
approach: Reformulates assembly as joint assembly-and-generation problem: generation informs structure via shape context while assembly provides part-level priors to generation.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance on in-the-wild objects with diverse geometries, varying part counts, and missing pieces; synthesizes complete shapes.

problem: Online link recommendation is performative—recommended links change future feedback and fairness estimates from logged outcomes become unreliable after policy updates.
approach: COPF defines group opportunity gaps over exposure counterfactuals, makes them estimable via explicit exploration and propensity logging, and audits with graph-aware doubly-robust estimators.
contribution: Reduces worst-case spikes in exposure-counterfactual disparities with modest ranking impact; includes residual outcome indistinguishability bounds under temporal mixing.

problem: Discovering causal structure in time series is difficult when systems have endogenous context variables that both drive dynamics and are influenced by system state.
approach: Introduces PCMCI-based algorithms for Structural Causal Models with endogenous discrete context variables, leveraging either context persistence or sparsity of dependencies.
contribution: Theoretically sound algorithms with proof of correctness; systematic evaluation on benchmarks and land-atmosphere feedback application demonstrates effectiveness.

problem: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction produces heuristic confidence scores lacking probabilistic grounding, failing to indicate where and how much predicted geometry can be trusted.
approach: Trust3R combines gated residual mean refinement with Normal-Inverse-Wishart evidential head to yield multivariate Student-t distribution for per-point uncertainty.
contribution: Achieves 25% lower AURC and 41% lower AUSE on ScanNet++; improves risk-coverage and sparsification across diverse indoor/outdoor benchmarks.

problem: Full-duplex voice agents are deployed to production but existing evaluations address conversational dynamics and task completion in isolation, not grounded complexity.
approach: tau-Voice extends tau-bench with voice agent evaluation combining verifiable task completion, full-duplex interaction, realistic audio, and controllable voice simulator.
contribution: Voice agents retain only 30-45% of text performance under realistic conditions; 79-90% of failures stem from agent behavior; provides reproducible testbed.

problem: Model-based RL world models either prioritize reconstruction fidelity without task relevance or focus on decision-critical features at the cost of dynamics quality.
approach: Value-Aligned World Model adds intrinsic latent-space value-alignment regularization with adaptive weighting that balances reconstruction fidelity and decision-making utility.
contribution: Consistently boosts existing methods on Atari 100k and DeepMind Control with minimal code overhead; provides unified framework with negligible computational cost.

problem: Learning dynamics of high-dimensional probability densities over time without trajectory information requires solving complex optimal transport couplings at each step.
approach: Two-parameter flows learn sampling-time transports from base to marginals, then extract physics-time velocity by regressing on synthetic trajectories; uniqueness guaranteed.
contribution: Scales to high dimensions while avoiding per-step transport couplings; naturally explains rotational or circulating physics phenomena.

problem: Learning optimal intervention sequences from offline data for online adaptive deployment remains challenging in domains like personalized medicine.
approach: GIFT learns goal-conditioned policy from observational data by rescaling rewards with clipped importance weights; converges to unique fixed point under standard assumptions.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in creating goal-conditioned policies; includes bias bounds from clipping and approximation.

problem: Physics-informed neural networks for time-dependent PDEs reuse a single network across all times, forcing same features to handle markedly different dynamics and destabilizing training.
approach: Time-Induced Neural Networks (TINNs) parameterizes network weights as learned functions of time, allowing spatial representation to evolve while maintaining shared structure.
contribution: Achieves up to 4× improved relative L2 error and 10× faster convergence compared to PINNs and baselines on various time-dependent PDEs.

problem: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning routing relies on sample-to-task similarity and equal cross-modal weighting, missing intra-task diversity and modality-specific reliability variation.
approach: Hyper-LLaVA models task matching in hyperbolic space to leverage intra-task diversity and quantifies per-modality matching ambiguity for adaptive cross-modal balancing.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA approaches by large margins on continual multimodal learning; addresses both intra- and inter-modality routing challenges.

problem: Aligning LLMs to serve heterogeneous, conflicting preferences while leveraging test-time compute through multi-sample generation remains theoretically uncharted.
approach: Formalizes universal alignment through test-time scaling and derives optimal convergence rates; shows symmetric multi-player alignment games preserve output diversity.
contribution: Characterizes optimal rate f(k)=k/(k+1) for k-sample policies; demonstrates methods like NLHF fundamentally underutilize test-time scaling due to diversity collapse.

problem: Rare events in LLMs—behavior far from typical but highly significant—are hard to observe during development yet likely to surface at scale during deployment.
approach: Develops end-to-end framework for systematic rare event analysis spanning theory, efficient generation strategies, probability estimation, and error analysis.
contribution: Provides practical implementation for analyzing rare events; generalizes to other models and contexts with concrete examples and extensions.

problem: Optimizing complex systems like LLM prompts and multi-turn agents requires labor-intensive manual iteration and struggles with stochastic feedback and solution space expansion.
approach: POLCA maintains priority queue for exploration-exploitation, uses epsilon-net for parameter diversity, and LLM Summarizer for meta-learning across trials.
contribution: Converges to near-optimal solutions under stochasticity; outperforms SOTA on tau-bench, HotpotQA, VeriBench, KernelBench with robust performance.

problem: Diffusion LLMs use fixed-size action blocks, creating rigidity that breaks logical reasoning flow and ignores task-specific optimal block size variation.
approach: b1 framework learns dynamic-size blocks via Monotonic Entropy Descent objective with RL, enforcing consistent descent across block entropies to ensure coherent reasoning.
contribution: Consistent improvement over fixed-size baselines on reasoning benchmarks; plug-and-play module for dLLM post-training with released code.

problem: Mamba-based 3D pose estimation struggles with forced sequence flattening confusion and depth modeling ambiguity from single-view observation.
approach: StructMamPose adds Identity Anchoring Mechanism to enforce valid topological dependencies and View Transformation Hub to transform depth inference into observable features.
contribution: Achieves SOTA on most datasets by addressing spatiotemporal modeling and explicit spatial understanding challenges.

problem: Grounding benchmark performance in human task completion time requires costly, noisy annotations that don't scale; pre-hoc prediction of this metric remains unexplored.
approach: BRIDGE uses Item Response Theory to jointly estimate latent task difficulty and model capability from performance data; aligns difficulty linearly with log(human time).
contribution: Infers human task completion time for new benchmarks from model performance; reproduces METR's exponential scaling with 50% horizon doubling every 6 months.

problem: Context-entangled content segmentation (camouflaged object detection) requires robust learning from data with unclear boundaries, where objects share patterns with surroundings.
approach: CurriSeg uses curriculum selection to distinguish hard-but-informative from noisy samples, then anti-curriculum fine-tuning via spectral-blindness and sharpness-aware minimization.
contribution: Consistent improvements across CECS benchmarks without added parameters or training time; unifies curriculum and anti-curriculum principles for robust segmentation.

problem: Coding agents excel at single GitHub issues but struggle to generalize across diverse real-world tasks requiring codebase exploration, testing, and architecture design.
approach: Hybrid-Gym provides scalable synthetic training tasks (function localization, dependency search) designed via decomposition of transferable skills across diverse coding tasks.
contribution: Improves base model by 25.4% on SWE-Bench Verified, 7.9% on SWT-Bench, 5.1% on Commit-0; complementary gains with downstream task datasets.

problem: LLM annealing phase relies on empirical heuristics for data selection that lack principled grounding in optimization theory.
approach: DiReCT characterizes annealing via loss landscape spectral geometry and formulates selection as constrained optimization with directional constraints on per-sample gradients.
contribution: Consistently achieves SOTA across model scales; identifies samples aligning with optimal curvature-aware descent path.

problem: Multimodal LLM self-improvement training suffers from data imbalance (simple samples over-trained, hard ones under-trained) and language prior bias neglecting visual cues.
approach: VISTA introduces prefix resampling to reuse partial correct traces and vision-aware attention scoring to quantify focus on visual information.
contribution: Brings up to +13.66% average gains across MLLMs and tasks; enhances both supervised fine-tuning and preference learning scenarios.

problem: Fixed-dimensional E(3)-equivariant latent spaces for 3D molecules are geometrically precise but semantically shallow for comprehensive representation learning.
approach: MolAlign3D anchors manipulable latents from MolFLAE with embeddings from pre-trained molecular encoder to create semantically dense and geometrically precise manifold.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and comparable property prediction; significantly enhances zero-shot molecular manipulation including atom-count editing.

problem: Feature-map knowledge distillation fails for ViT compression despite per-image compressibility—revealed through spectral analysis as an encoding mismatch.
approach: Identifies bandwidth mismatch where tokens spread energy across modes even in low-rank subspace; proposes Lift (lightweight inference projector) or WideLast (wider last block).
contribution: Revives feature KD for ViT compression, improving DeiT-Tiny distilled from CaiT-S24 from 74.86% to 77.53%/78.23% top-1 accuracy.

problem: Video diffusion model adversarial attacks via image-to-video conditioning fail because robust spatio-temporal priors suppress motion artifact injection.
approach: MEDUSA targets temporal attention matrix rank collapse via nuclear norm minimization, inducing degenerate rank-1 state to freeze video motion.
contribution: Achieves effective motion elimination validated by mathematical analysis; circumvents gradient vanishing in direct temporal mapping.

problem: LLM-based CAD generation lacks high-quality datasets, fine-grained evaluation, and doesn't adequately decompose geometric vs. spatial reasoning in multi-step modeling.
approach: Op-CAD introduces largest operation-oriented CAD dataset with parsing module and geometry-guided annotation; proposes Chamfer/Fillet IoU metric and Chain-of-Operation prompting.
contribution: Establishes benchmark across eight LLMs; Chain-of-Operation strategy improves results by emulating human-engineer step-by-step reasoning.

problem: Pre-hoc performance prediction for fine-tuning remains theoretically ungrounded; understanding fundamental prediction limits is unclear.
approach: Decomposes risk into intrinsic limit (static compatibility) and reducible optimization variance; proves variance admits necessary decay-rate bound and derives budget-optimal probing.
contribution: Derives predictability phase diagram organizing tasks into Static-Sufficient, Dynamic-Critical, and Noise-Dominant regimes; validates on synthetic and real benchmarks.

problem: Best-of-N selection in LLMs relies on unreliable verification—logit confidence suffers calibration collapse while sample agreement is costly and brittle.
approach: Analyzes latent dynamics during inference and introduces Latent Velocity Entropy (LVE), a training-free metric quantifying temporal concentration of representation updates.
contribution: On MATH500, LogNorm-LVE reaches 92.2% Pass@1 at N=10 with only 3 samples; remains informative when logit-confidence fails on reasoning tasks.

problem: Formal mathematics in Lean lacks many folklore lemmas that mathematicians take for granted, limiting usability for everyday mathematical work.
approach: MathlibLemma mines missing connective tissue via modular LLM pipeline: discovery, formalization, and proving of reusable intermediate facts.
contribution: Produces 1,506 Lean-checked proofs with 4,028-statement benchmark; curated subset merged into Mathlib; transforms LLMs from passive to active library contributors.

problem: Data science agent benchmarks have fragmented interfaces, narrow coverage, and lack rigorous data grounding—many tasks solvable without using actual data.
approach: DSGym provides standardized modular framework with quality-filtered tasks, adds DSBio (expert bioinformatics) and DSPredict (challenging prediction), and execution-verified synthesis.
contribution: Enables end-to-end measurement of agent planning, implementation, and validation; training on 2,000 examples substantially improves 4B model on benchmarks.

problem: Federated LoRA suffers from rotational misalignment—semantically equivalent updates represented in different latent subspaces across clients interfere destructively when averaged.
approach: FedRot-LoRA aligns client updates via orthogonal transformations before aggregation to reduce cross-client subspace mismatch without communication cost.
contribution: Convergence analysis shows alignment yields tighter aggregation error bounds; consistently outperforms baselines across heterogeneity levels without restricting expressivity.
